BREAKING: Samsung reportedly plans to make chips for SpaceX’s Starlink satellites in Austin, Texas. 

Samsung is investing $1.9 billion to expand its Austin chip factory, with the planned operations targeted to begin by 2030, according to Seoul Economic Daily.

The chip, called STM32V8, is already used in Starlink’s mini laser system. SpaceX’s Starlink engineering team has praised the chip’s performance.

The chips are currently manufactured in France. The reported Texas plan would add American production capacity for a key component behind Starlink’s satellite communications.

An anonymous source reports alleged new info about the GTA 6 review copies Rockstar sent to journalists:

- There are apparently no Xbox review copies because Xbox’s review process doesn’t meet Rockstar’s security expectations
- Reviewers weren’t given game codes. Instead, Rockstar worked with PlayStation to assign the game directly to a specific PSN account on a specific console
- Claims about gameplay watermarks are false and Rockstar is tracking potential leaks through a different, much smarter method
- Microsoft employees may still have access to Xbox copies for testing, certification, or other internal purposes, just not reviews
- Some Xbox content creators complained about not receiving Xbox review copies. Rockstar’s response was essentially: “Ask your Microsoft contacts why”

PSN security:
- Last month a group of hackers compiled a list of accounts they believed had access to the game but they were unsuccessful
- They reportedly managed to access one account but it was completely blocked from connecting to PSN when used on another console
- Rockstar and Sony have added extra security measures that link review copies to either an IP address or a console serial number
- If someone tries to access the account from a different IP address or console, it gets locked out and Sony is alerted

(via @PorkPoncho)

New GTA 6 details from The Guardian’s preview at Rockstar North:

- It’s the first title in the series to encourage empathy, as your actions will have some effect on how the game plays out
- You can rob high-end shops in a shopping mall
- A lot of devs have finished working on the game a month before release and are taking a well deserved rest after 10+ years of development
- Rockstar says they could’ve made GTA 5.5 and done it faster but that’s not what they wanted: “You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same,” says Rob Nelson
- Rockstar says the game is really hard to close down because they always want to add more, but they reached the point where it needs to be finalized and released
- There are 62 types of birds you can record in a wildlife logbook and observe them through binoculars
- Every NPC you see has been designed by someone, even down to their clothes
- Tech limits are no longer the problem for Rockstar but it’s now the human resources and how much the team can build, simply throwing money at a game doesn’t guarantee it will be good

(via The Guardian / @GameRoll_)
